newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi customs workers threaten strike from Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Malawi customs workers threaten strike from Tuesday.

text.p: Malawi's Customs Workers Union (CWU), representing 80 percent of the government's total revenue, has threatened to join a month-old civil servant strike from Tuesday.

The CWU said in a statement to the president's office on Sunday that its members would join the strike unless the government reinstated all dismissed workers, restrained police from arresting striking workers and paid arrears in wages from January to April this year.
The workers are taking part in a nationwide strike called by the Civil Servants' Trade Union to push for a 100 percent wage increase as recommended by an independent commission.
The government has said it could only afford a 47 percent pay increase for its 100,000-strong workforce without upsetting the economy.
It has issued some workers with dismissal notices and has suspended others without pay, altogether affecting an estimated 200 staff so far.

"Due to government's intransigence and non-committal (stance) to negotiations, the Customs Workers Union has unanimously agreed to go on strike for three days starting from 6th May 1997," the statement said.
"...If government does not show any willingness to do what we have asked it to do, then two more days shall be added on," the union said.
CWU Secretary General Honeck Kampini told Reuters that passengers arriving at the country's biggest airport would be allowed free entry.
However, hauliers and other travellers at the main borders would not be allowed entry or exit, he said.
"There, we're saying there should be total blockade. Maybe people will have to find their way, maybe through bush roads. We are determined. We're set. Tuesday we are closing the borders.
"Our members will be at the offices in full uniform as usual but they'll not be rendering services." Kampini said.
